newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TVB forecast to show healthy earnings.
newsitem.headline: TVB forecast to show healthy earnings.

text.p: Hong Kong's largest broadcasting company, Television Broadcasts Ltd, is expected to unveil a healthy improvement in earnings when it releases its first half 1996 results on Wednesday, analysts said.

TVB, which saw profit margins and earnings plummet in 1995, was forecast to report earning growth of around 20 percent for the full year, with interim profit growth just slightly slower, analysts said.

"Earnings will be boosted by rising contribution from some of its overseas joint ventures. We are forecasting earnings of HK$585 million for 1996, a growth of 22.4 percent," said Andrew Farrant, media analyst at SBC Warburg Asia Ltd.
The interims may show slightly slower growth, Farrant said.
"In 1995, the company suffered a fall in earnings due to a downturn in advertising expenditure felt by all sectors of the media," said Robert Fong, media analyst at HSBC James Capel Asia Ltd.

The chief boost to earnings this year, however, will be advertising and sponsorship revenue associated with the 1996 Olympics, the airing of which was shared by both TVB and its Hong Kong terrestrial rival Asia Television Ltd.
"Advertising revenue earned from the broadcasting of the Olympics, of course, will be realised in the second half," said Fong.
HSBC's Fong is forecasting earnings growth of 17.4 percent to HK$570 million in all of 1996 and more rapid growth of 21.4 percent in all of 1997.
Net profit estimates from analysts range from HK$531 million to HK$656 million, or an average increase of 22 percent for 1996.
Analysts declined to give interim forecasts.
Farrant said he recommends a weak buy for the stock despite its current high rating of about 21 times 1996 earnings.
"TVB is currently trading at about a 40 percent premium to the market but we believe this is justified," he said.
"The company is becoming a regional media play. As such it should be compared to other comparable listed companies in Asia and Europe and deserving of a re-rating," he added.
Fong, on the other hand, recommends a sell. "While the company has certainly laid the groundwork to establish itself as a regional player, profitability may still be a few years away," he said.
"At current price levels, the company's dominant market position in Hong Kong and its regional growth potential have already been discounted," he added.
